This deep Wolfcamp stack target — one of the highest TVD wells Permian Resources has permitted in 2026 — will require a high-performance synthetic-base or advanced water-base system capable of 230°F+ stability, a spec that narrows the field and elevates your pitch if you can offer HPHT-qualified fluids. Permian Resources has been actively renegotiating fluid MSAs following their merger integration, making this an unusually open competitive cycle — engage their Midland drilling manager before September 15 when pre-spud planning meetings are scheduled.

SandRidge's Mississippi Lime horizontal in Woods County is a shallower, cost-sensitive program where Conquest has priced competitively before, but Newpark and National Oilwell Varco's fluid division have been circling this operator with aggressive Q4 proposals. Engaging SandRidge's field operations manager in Woodward before September 20 keeps you ahead of competing Q4 bids.

Liberty Resources is a smaller independent with limited long-term vendor commitments, making them highly persuadable on price and local inventory availability for this Burke County location. Engaging now—seven weeks before spud—gives you the full procurement window to displace Tetra Technologies, which currently provides completion brines but has a weaker drilling-fluids footprint in the northwest corner of the basin.

Berry's shallower Muddy J target in Morgan County is early in the pre-spud cycle with an early-October spud estimate, giving a narrow but real opportunity to influence the fluids selection before a formal RFQ is issued around August 25-28. Newpark has historically served Berry's DJ shallow program, but the relatively low complexity of Muddy J wells makes this a price-sensitive opportunity where a well-timed value proposal could displace the incumbent.

Aethon's GRB division is newly formed after their 2025 acreage acquisition and has no cemented mud vendor relationship in Wyoming, making this permit-fresh well the highest-upside open opportunity in the basin right now. Contact their Casper operations lead immediately—permit ink is barely dry and no preferred vendor has been named.

Tellurian's permit in Panola County, TX was filed just three days ago and no mud contract has been awarded—this is the earliest possible entry point in the sales cycle before any competitor is engaged. Newpark Resources is the most likely awardee given their Carthage-area logistics infrastructure, but the account is fully open to a competing proposal through at least early September.

Devon's newly permitted LaSalle County location is freshly issued today and the mud vendor selection process has almost certainly not begun, giving any competitor a clean-slate opportunity. Baroid has the regional infrastructure advantage, but a proactive technical proposal submitted this week could anchor the conversation before Baroid's local rep mobilizes.
